verses.text: [“]Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.

xrefs.text: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
[“]Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?

verses.text: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.

xrefs.text: A voice says, “Cry out!” And I asked, “What should I cry out?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.
For, “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,
For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
As for man, his days are like grass— he blooms like a flower of the field;
You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

verses.text: Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?

xrefs.text: O LORD, what is man, that You regard him, the son of man that You think of him?
Do not bring Your servant into judgment, for no one alive is righteous before You.
what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.

verses.text: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!

xrefs.text: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.
What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
All of us also lived among them at one time, fulfilling the cravings of our flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts. Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath.
Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

verses.text: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,

xrefs.text: “Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days. Let me know how fleeting my life is.
From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,
When You hide Your face, they are terrified; when You take away their breath, they die and return to dust.

verses.text: look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.

xrefs.text: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?
Turn Your gaze away from me, that I may again be cheered before I depart and am no more.”
[“]Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,
I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

verses.text: For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.

xrefs.text: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.

And you, O king, saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying: ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, with a band of iron and bronze around it, in the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and graze with the beasts of the field till seven times pass him by.’
He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.

verses.text: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,

xrefs.text: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.

verses.text: at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.

xrefs.text: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,
Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant waters.

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.

verses.text: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?

xrefs.text: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,

verses.text: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,

xrefs.text: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.
But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow,
Why is my pain unending, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have indeed become like a mirage to me— water that is not there.

verses.text: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.

xrefs.text: before I go— never to return— to a land of darkness and gloom,
For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other— they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. The heavens will disappear with a roar, the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and its works will be laid bare.

verses.text: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!

xrefs.text: Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.
No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; devout men are taken away, while no one considers that the righteous are taken away from the presence of evil.
For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.
There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.

verses.text: When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.

xrefs.text: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—
[“]Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!
Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,

verses.text: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.

xrefs.text: The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands.
Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.
Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?

verses.text: For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.

xrefs.text: that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin—
Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. O LORD, You have searched me and known me.
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.

verses.text: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.

xrefs.text: “Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?
The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.
It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.

verses.text: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,

xrefs.text: The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place.
You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.
Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them.
Then the second angel sounded his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned to blood,

verses.text: as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.

xrefs.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished— birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, ‘Our bones are dried up, and our hope has perished; we are cut off.’

verses.text: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.

xrefs.text: But now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as a stick.
As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.

verses.text: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.

xrefs.text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
Yet You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, O LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from Everlasting is Your name.
I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Surely every man goes about like a phantom; surely he bustles in vain; he heaps up riches not knowing who will haul them away.

verses.text: He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”

My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones,
The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
